messages:
maria: quick thread—thinking about frontdoor behavior when we fan a single client request to multiple upstreams (hedging / A/B). do we try to preserve response ordering for streaming responses or treat them as independent and accept the first complete/fastest? :thinking:
jonathan: IMO first-success wins for single-response RPCs. for streaming we need to pick: either preserve monotonic token order (hard) or allow midstream cutoff with a clear client-visible signal. preserving order means we buffer and potentially add latency.
beth: buffering seem risky for latency-sensitive use cases. could we offer two modes: `ordered_streaming = true|false` in route config? default to false.
alex: agree on two modes. need to surface guarantees in SDKs and on the wire. if ordered, we should attach an `x-frontdoor-order-hint` and maintain per-request seq metadata so downstream can verify continuity.
nina: what about idempotency / side-effects when hedging? if we send the same request to two upstreams and both process it, we need at-least-once semantics unless upstreams dedupe. we should require idempotency-token for hedged calls with side-effects. add validation in frontdoor to reject hedging if no token and route marked side_effect=true.
maria: good call. also for streaming, hedging midstream is nasty: you can get duplicated partial tokens. maybe we should only hedge at request start or at well-defined chunk boundaries (trailer checkpoints).
jonathan: agreed — define a hedging window: hedges can be issued only before first non-empty chunk or at explicit checkpoint (client includes `stream-checkpoint: <n>`). implementation: frontdoor waits for checkpoint boundary before switching upstreams.
beth: can we expose a graceful cutoff trailer like `x-stream-cutoff: reason=hedge;cut_at_token=123` so clients know tokens past that point are discarded? SDKs can stitch.
edge-bot: deploy note: canary for `hedge-checkpoint` feature landing in prod in 2h to route `beta/ordered_streams`. monitor latency/dup-token metrics.
alex: ops question — how do we handle backpressure if ordered==true and upstream B starts producing while A is slow? buffering could blow memory. propose soft-buffer cap per-req (configurable) + spill to disk / abort with `413 StreamBufferExceeded` back to client.
nina: fallback behavior: if buffer cap hit and ordered mode, we should either degrade to unordered mode (if route allows) or return an explicit failover message so client can retry with unordered flag.
maria: propose RFC follow-up: API for routes: `ordered_streaming`, `hedge_policy {type: start|checkpoint, max_hedges, idempotency_required}` and `buffer_limits {tokens, bytes, spill:true|false}`. add observability: per-request hedged_count, buffered_tokens, cutoff_reason.
jonathan: sounds good. small nit: default `idempotency_required=true` when `hedge_policy.max_hedges>0` to protect side-effects. document expectations for SDKs (auto-add idempotency-token unless user overrides).
beth: also add a cost note: hedging midstream multiplies token billing. we should emit a billing tag `x-bill-hedged` per-token so cost attribution is clear.
alex: I'll draft a strawman config and basic state machine for a follow-up RFC. cc @maria @jonathan for review.
maria: thanks — add a couple of examples: short-poll RPCs (unordered, hedge=start) vs long chat streams (ordered, hedge=checkpoint). quick thumbs? :+1:
jonathan: +1
beth: +1
nina: +1
edge-bot: monitor alert created: `hedge-buffer-exceeded` on prod canary group.
